question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=8x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=8y(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(0) \\ y(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].$*
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,x(0),
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $x(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5t{e}^{8t} \\ 5{e}^{8t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
